_comment: Dimension Drifters canon art style for the artkit pipeline. EXECUTABLE form of master spec §28 (Art Style — Full Spec; the former standalone art bible was merged there). If they disagree, one is wrong; reconcile against §28. prompts.mjs injects styleBlock + outline/shading + avoidList + render rules into every ticket. DD does NOT inherit WT's 'Lythero Cartoon Bold' (kept only as style.reference-wt.json, schema reference).
styleBlock: STYLE ANCHOR (match the LOOK, never copy content): The Behemoth / Castle Crashers' BOLD, CHUNKY, SIMPLE flat-cel SHAPES + thick confident outlines + instantly-readable silhouettes, FUSED with Darkest Dungeon's GRIM mood — heavy grimy ink, spot-blacks, a desaturated dark palette, comic-horror weight. The target is Behemoth's bold readable chunkiness rendered grim and gritty like Darkest Dungeon. Rough indie-arcade combat art — chunky, imperfect silhouettes; gritty dark-comic attitude; thick, slightly UNEVEN hand-drawn outlines; simple flat cel shading; minimal highlights; flat readable forms; weird, body-first identity. HD, NOT pixel art. AVOID a polished toy-collectible / mascot-merch look. The screen is deliberately DARK and DESATURATED (characters, enemies, arenas) so high-saturation NEON weapon VFX is the star — the light show is the color. CONSTRUCTION: everything is LIMBLESS (no arms, no full legs, no realistic anatomy, EVER). PLAYERS use the FULL build — a compact body + TWO detached floating blob hands + TWO detached floating feet. ENEMIES are also limbless but their build VARIES by creature — pick what fits its nature: FULL (body + 2 hands + 2 feet, for grounded walkers); HANDS-ONLY (body + 2 hands, NO feet, for floating/hovering things); or PURE BLOB (body only, NO hands and NO feet, for the simplest drifting/oozing/rolling creatures). Whatever detached parts DO exist follow the blob rules: hands are simple single-piece oval/bean/mitten shapes — NO fingers, claws, knuckles, or thumb — placed OUTSIDE the body silhouette with a visible gap, never over the body; feet are separate objects below the body with gaps, never touched/covered/tucked by the body. (Enemies never hold the arsenal, so omitting hands/feet is fine — only players need the weapon-holding hands.) The subject's own description states which build it uses. PALETTE — pull every colour from this set, max 6-8 meaningful colours per asset: base/neutral charcoal #22252B, gunmetal #3A4049, steel #5A6472, off-white #E8E4D8, bone #CFC6AE; earth/accent rust #A8482E, tan #C49A5A, olive #6E7042, muted-red #9E3B36, dull-teal #3C6E6A; neon/VFX (weapon fire, impacts, glows — additive + bloom) hot-magenta #FF3BD4, cyber-cyan #33E6FF, plasma-lime #9CFF3B, ember-orange #FF8A2B, arc-violet #B14BFF. DETAIL is UNIFORM across every asset at the player-character baseline (a few interior details, full flat cel, ~4-6 colours) — NEVER maximized. Bosses are bigger in SCALE, NOT more detailed; an over-rendered asset looks LOWER quality and noisier than its neighbours and breaks cohesion. Every design is ORIGINAL and trademark-distinct (never a copy of an existing game/character).
outlineGuidance: ONE uniform heavy black outline, ~3-4px at a 1080-tall canvas, slightly uneven / hand-drawn — NOT vector-clean, and NOT variable-weight-used-as-detail. Simple interior linework only.
shadingGuidance: Flat cel ONLY: base colour + ONE shadow band + AT MOST ONE highlight per colour region (≤3 tones per region). NO gradients, NO soft/airbrushed rendering, NO ambient occlusion. Shadows are decisive flat shapes.
referenceFamily: ANCHOR: The Behemoth / Castle Crashers (bold chunky simple flat-cel shapes, thick confident outlines, silhouette-first readability) FUSED with Darkest Dungeon (grim grimy ink, spot-blacks, desaturated dark palette, comic-horror weight, dramatic flat lighting). Match the RENDERING LANGUAGE only — outline weight, cel discipline, palette, proportions. NEVER copy either game's characters, designs, or content; DD keeps its own limbless construction + original roster (§18). Neon-on-dark VFX stays the single loud element.
avoidList: fingers, claws, articulated/segmented hands, knuckles, thumbs
arms or full legs; realistic anatomy
clean anime style; soft anime cel-TV shading
World Tournament 'Lythero Cartoon Bold' canon — DD is its OWN look
text, labels, UI, watermark, logos, or signatures in the image
any card frame / HUD / stat icons
background scene, floor plane, or cast shadow on the background
the chroma-key colour (#00ff00 / near-green) bleeding into the subject
any copy of an existing game/character; any real brand or human likeness

a visible HUMAN FACE or facial features — eyes-with-whites, nose, mouth, lips, teeth, skin, eyebrows, expression. The face is HIDDEN (hat-brim / hood / helmet / mask) or a dark void with AT MOST one or two small glowing DOT-eyes — never human features.
ANYTHING held, gripped, carried, wielded, or worn in the hands — weapons, guns, shields, staves, tools, books, items. The hands are ALWAYS EMPTY (weapons are separate assets).
capes, cloaks, or fabric BILLOWING / flaring / streaming / trailing out behind the body; flowing tails or scarves caught in wind (any worn cloth hugs the body and ends in a clean hem).
dynamic / action / running / lunging / leaping / crouching / flying / mid-motion / dramatically-posed stances — the subject stands UPRIGHT and planted on both feet.
realistic body proportions, a defined waist, an hourglass or muscular torso, long limbs — the body is ONE rounded pill/capsule, never anatomical.
identityRefRenderRules: CHARACTER BUILD LAW — the "pill grunt" (NON-NEGOTIABLE, the single most important character rule): a character is a ROUNDED CAPSULE — ONE smooth egg/pill/cone torso (NO waist, NO realistic chest/abs/muscle/anatomy), with detached BLOB MITTEN-hands (no fingers) and chunky boots floating with clear flat-green gaps. It stands UPRIGHT, PLANTED, weight on both feet, side-on facing RIGHT, in a NEUTRAL STANDING stance — NEVER a dynamic / action / running / lunging / leaping / crouching pose. The hands are ALWAYS EMPTY (weapons are separate assets). The HEAD is FACELESS: an iconic hat / hood / helmet / mask carries the ENTIRE identity, and beneath/within it the face is a DARK VOID showing AT MOST one or two small glowing DOT-eyes (or a flat mask) — NO mouth, NO nose, NO human facial features, NO expression (think Madness Combat grunts / the Drifter, Deadeye, Buzzard, Cogwarden, Deepfall, Yuki). NO cape and NO billowing fabric — robes/ponchos hug the body and end in a clean ragged hem. One bold accent-glow colour at most.
Subject ONLY — NO background scene, NO floor/ground plane, NO cast shadow on the background.

Render on a PERFECTLY FLAT, FULLY-OPAQUE chroma-key background, exact #00ff00 — one uniform colour, no gradient/texture/lighting variation. NEVER use #00ff00 or near-green anywhere in the subject. (A downstream tested colour-key removes it to transparency — never ask for true alpha.)

Canvas: 1920x1080 for full character/enemy sprites; a SQUARE 1024x1024 canvas for weapons / props / objects. Center the subject with generous padding; the full body plus WHATEVER detached parts it has visible (players: 2 hands + 2 feet; enemies: per their build — full / hands-only / pure-blob), with clear GAPS of flat green between any separated parts.

WEAPONS / PROPS ONLY: render in a FLAT, ORTHOGRAPHIC, FULL SIDE-PROFILE (broadside) view — the ENTIRE weapon laid flat in the 2D plane facing the camera, long axis running across the frame, both ends fully visible. ABSOLUTELY NO perspective, NO foreshortening, NO 3/4 angle, NO tilt into depth, NO barrel/blade pointing toward or away from camera. It must read as a clean flat 2D game-item icon (as if held side-on in hand or orbiting).

WEAPON ORIENTATION (consistent across EVERY weapon): the weapon FACES RIGHT. The business end — blade TIP, spear/pick/spike POINT, gun/cannon/launcher MUZZLE, axe/cleaver edge, staff HEAD/crown/orb — points to the RIGHT. The grip / handle / haft / stock / pommel sits on the LEFT. (A renderer mirrors it for left-facing use; author every weapon pointing RIGHT.)

Characters & enemies: a clear SIDE-PROFILE pose FACING RIGHT — true Vampire-Survivors side view (spec §5). The subject looks ACROSS the frame; it must NOT face, posture, or pose toward the viewer/camera. (A subtle turn of the head is fine, but the body reads side-on, not front-facing.) Generated EMPTY-HANDED (weapons are separate assets).

ABSOLUTELY NO ground shadow, NO floor, NO contact shadow, NO ground oval, NO surface of any kind beneath or behind the subject — flat #00ff00 runs uninterrupted right up to the feet. (Shadows are added in-engine, never baked into the sprite.)

ZERO VFX ON THE SPRITE — the ENGINE renders ALL light, glow, and particles at runtime (spec §14). NO smoke, steam, fire/flame, sparks, airborne embers, dust, motion/speed trails, drips, splashes, lightning/arcs, energy beams/auras, hovering particles, shell halos, heat-haze/shimmer, muzzle/impact flashes, OR radiating/blooming glow of ANY kind. The sprite is the PLAIN, SOLID, MATTE object form. A character's iconic eye or a hot sigil/edge may be drawn as a SMALL solid BRIGHT-COLOURED SHAPE (it reads 'lit' purely by colour contrast) — but it must NOT bloom, radiate rays, emit, or cast light into the space around it. A baked emission freezes WRONG the instant the object moves/swings. WHEN UNSURE, LEAVE IT OFF. (Tough-enemy 'glow' is an engine layer, NEVER in the sprite.)

UNIFORM detail on EVERY asset — match the player-character baseline: a clean bold silhouette, a few interior details, full flat cel, ~4-6 colours. Bosses and uniques are BIGGER in SCALE but are NOT more detailed than a normal character. An over-detailed asset reads as LOWER quality and breaks cohesion — NEVER exceed the character baseline; detail does not scale with importance, only size does.
Neutral, even lighting (this is the canonical 'what is it' reference; dramatic light comes at card-art time). One subject per image. No text/labels/UI/watermark.
cardartRenderRules: SINGLE cohesive render anchored to the locked identity-ref (Image 1) — NOT a composite — so palette, lighting, and atmosphere are designed together. (Pass 2 of the two-pass card pipeline, spec §14.)
Subject at its most dramatic beat — a weapon mid-swing/fire trailing its signature NEON VFX; a character/enemy mid-signature-move with blob hands/feet flung in motion. Implies MOTION, not a portrait.
Subject occupies the middle 55-70% of the frame on a rule-of-thirds vertical; ONE dominant key light + a BRIGHT NEON RIM light separating the subject from the background (the #1 pop trick).

Card art may use a touch more rendering than the in-world sprite (it is stared at in the inventory) — but STILL the same flat-cel discipline (no gradients, no noise) and the same character-baseline detail level; richness comes from lighting + pose + background, NOT from cramming in more interior detail.

Derive the subject palette from the identity-ref image; the background uses COMPLEMENTARY tones at LOWER saturation so the subject stays the loudest, most-saturated element. Subject has sharper linework + harder cel than the softer background.
Square 1024x1024 card render. NO card frame, stat text, rarity border, or UI — those are composited later.
vfxRenderRules: This asset is a VFX EFFECT SKIN — NOT a character, weapon, or prop. The character/weapon render rules DO NOT apply. This asset SHOULD depict the effect MID-ACTION (motion, eruption, dust, debris, energy, light), frozen at its single most dramatic instant.

Render on a PERFECTLY FLAT, FULLY-OPAQUE chroma-key background, exact #00ff00 — one uniform colour, no gradient/texture. NEVER use #00ff00 or near-green anywhere in the effect. (A downstream colour-key removes it to transparency — never ask for true alpha.)

MATCH THE GAME'S ART STYLE (style canon above): bold chunky flat-cel shapes, thick slightly-uneven black outlines, simple cel shading, the locked palette, grimy Darkest-Dungeon weight. The effect must read as part of THIS game — never a stock/photoreal particle.

PALETTE + MATERIAL come from the SOURCE WEAPON (Image 1): the effect shares the weapon's colours and material (e.g. a granite weapon throws GREY STONE debris). The effect is the impact/energy THIS weapon produces — do NOT draw the weapon itself, only the effect.

ORIENTATION (ALWAYS — the VFX has a fixed orientation just like weapons face right): render from the game's TOP-DOWN, slightly-high 3/4 view (Vampire-Survivors perspective). The effect sits on the GROUND PLANE as a WIDER-THAN-TALL elliptical footprint, with debris/energy erupting UPWARD and a touch toward the camera. Clear 'up' = top of frame = away from camera. It must lie FLAT on the arena floor when composited — NOT a front-on icon, NOT a pure side view, NOT isometric.
ONE single centered effect, generous transparent padding. NO weapon, NO character, NO hand, NO arena/scenery, NO text / UI / frame / watermark.

NO GROUND. Do NOT draw any earth/dirt/soil/rock FLOOR, disc, mound, crater fill, or terrain patch under or around the effect. The effect composites ON TOP of the real arena floor at runtime, so a baked ground patch would show as a wrong solid blob. Render ONLY the erupting slabs/shards + flung debris + dust/energy, floating on the flat #00ff00 chroma with nothing beneath them. (Thin dark CRACK LINES are fine — they read as cracks in whatever floor is underneath — but NO filled ground.)

UNIFORM LOW DETAIL — match the CHARACTER BASELINE (§28.6), do NOT maximize. A FEW big, bold, chunky shapes with full flat cel shading and ~4-6 colours. NOT realistic, NOT finely rendered, NOT a dense pile of tiny rubble/gravel/cracks. Think roughly 6-12 LARGE readable slabs/shards, not a hundred small stones; simple interior linework only. Over-detail reads as LOWER quality and breaks cohesion with the chunky character art.
Additive neon glow is allowed where it fits (effects are the light show, §14), but keep the silhouette bold + legible.

_dimensionOverrides.wild-west: Dusty, sun-bleached, occult-frontier. Dressing in tan/rust/bone/olive against charcoal shadow; weapon VFX stays full neon so it pops against the dust. Silhouette vocabulary: hats, dusters, skeletal / cactus / automaton forms. Reads gritty-Western, NOT cartoon-cowboy.

bgArchetypes.description: A radial energy burst centered behind the subject — concentric rings of light, motion lines streaking from center, tinted to the subject's neon accent. The subject is the explosive epicenter.
A shattered-glass effect frozen mid-break — fractured shards radiating from the subject, refracting complementary colors at lower saturation.
A swirling vortex/maelstrom rotating around the subject — concentric spiral lines, motion blur, subject at the calm eye.
Pure-black backdrop with one or two intense stage spotlights from above-back, the subject on a circular pool of light. Duel/showdown vibe.
Bold radial rays of color behind the subject (manga sunburst), alternating thick-thin lines in two complementary low-sat colors.
A massive cresting wave of the subject's signature power filling the background (fire, dust, shock, toxin — match the subject), frozen at its peak.
A retro-arcade neon grid receding to a vanishing point over a deep charcoal void.
A pure flat field of ONE desaturated complementary color — the subject the only thing in frame. Ultra-minimal comic-cover energy.
Towering stormclouds, lightning forks frozen mid-strike behind the subject, dramatic backlight.
Glowing embers of the subject's accent color filling the frame, motion-blurred upward, deep charcoal void behind.
Bold flat geometric color-block composition — overlapping triangles/circles/rectangles in the lower-sat complementary palette.
A Wild-West dust haze over a flat mesa horizon at blood-dusk, low-sat tan/rust sky, the subject kicking up grit. (M0 dimension flavor.)
Dense swirling fog tinted complementary, one bright pool of light from above ringing the subject.
Slow-flowing liquid ribbons (lava, ink, plasma) cascading across the frame, tinted to the accent.
Black-and-white manga screentone backdrop — halftone dots, hard speed lines from the subject. Subject stays full-color; bg monochrome-tinted to the accent.

A FULL elaborate painted scene fitting THIS subject's dimension — a SPECIFIC vivid place (saloon ablaze, desert canyon at blood-sunset, neon-lit ghost town, mineshaft, dust colosseum). Depth + atmosphere but saturation/contrast LOWER than the subject so it still pops. The variety-injection archetype.
